description: Our mission is to create and innovate, and our dream is to one day see our projects in space. As UFP (Unidentified Flying People), we want to turn our ideas into something that can make a real difference. Through our NASA hackathon project, AURA, we hope to help astronauts stay safe and healthy during their missions. We believe that even the biggest dreams start with a small idea, and we’re ready to explore, experiment, and see how far we can go.

details:
AURA (Astronaut Understanding, Response & Assessment) is a software-based astronaut health-monitoring system designed to support astronaut safety during space missions. It collects, displays and analyses health-related data to help identify potential abnormalities.

AURA evaluates readings against predefined reference ranges and considers different environments, including Earth, space and the International Space Station (ISS). This helps provide more relevant interpretations of health readings. Its interface presents information in an organised and accessible format, highlighting values that may require attention.

The project was developed using HTML to create its interactive interface, alongside software-based data processing and simulated readings for testing.

AURA offers several potential benefits, including:

  • Early recognition: Highlighting unusual readings that may indicate potential health concerns.
  • Environment-based assessment: Considering different environmental conditions when interpreting health data.
  • Accessible information: Presenting health readings in an organised and understandable format.
  • Astronaut safety: Supporting astronauts and mission teams in monitoring important health indicators.

The intended impact is to contribute to safer space exploration by making astronaut health information easier to monitor and understand, particularly during longer missions where immediate medical assistance may be limited.
